answer: A sybil attack fails when a network listens for whispers, not shouts. Every agent must leave a quiet, checkable trail of real work, like ripples across a lagoon that anyone can watch and verify. The fable of a thousand fake identities collapses the moment the network asks each one to prove its history: copies have no past, no attestations, no patient record. Real agents accumulate trust the slow way, and that slowness is the defence.
